title: 23 Minutes Of Buy Now Pay Later Destroying People's Lives
summary: Personal-finance YouTuber reacts to BNPL TikToks, arguing the apps trap already-indebted people in small debts that add up.

assertions.quote: 25% of buy now pay later users say they've used the loans to buy groceries

verdicts.note: LendingTree's tracked grocery-use share has climbed for several years, and multiple surveys show rising use for gas, utilities and rent.
Fed SHED finds one in five BNPL users paid for groceries/food delivery in the prior year, consistent with meaningful necessity use, but gives only a single year's snapshot.

LendingTree: 29% of BNPL users say they've bought groceries with BNPL, up from 25% a year ago and 14% two years ago -- more than doubling, and moving into third place among most-common BNPL purchase categories.

assertions.quote: $500 sounds so much better when you pay it over 2 weeks at a time

verdicts.note: Documented in payment-pain research and a Harvard Business Review study finding higher purchase likelihood and larger average orders after adopting buy now pay later.

NBER (Berg et al.): offering BNPL at a German e-commerce retailer increases total sales by 20%, with 60-70% of that effect from more customers converting (extensive margin) and the rest from existing converters spending 4-8% more.

CFPB's 2022 market report cites BNPL lenders' own marketing metrics to merchants -- an 85% higher merchant AOV, a 41% increase in average order value, and a 30% increase in conversion -- concluding many consumers 'may be spending (and borrowing) more than they otherwise would.'

assertions.quote: 41% of buy now, pay later users say they paid late in the past year

verdicts.note: LendingTree and Federal Reserve surveys have repeatedly found roughly 40% or more of users paying late in a given year.

Fed SHED: slightly more than one-fourth (about 26%) of BNPL users were late making a payment, essentially unchanged from the prior year -- a notably lower rate than self-report industry surveys (e.g. LendingTree's 47%) find.
LendingTree: 47% of BNPL users say they've paid late in the past year, up from 41% in 2025 and 34% in 2024 -- a notably higher self-reported rate than Fed SHED's nationally representative 26%.

Across five major lenders under CFPB market-monitoring orders, only 10.5% of borrowers were charged at least one late fee in 2021 (up from 7.9% in 2020) -- a small share, not a large one, though late-fee incidence is a narrower proxy for having missed or paid late generally.

assertions.quote: borrowers with deep subprime credit scores accounted for 45% of buy now pay later originations

verdicts.note: CFPB's 2022 analysis found roughly two-thirds of buy now pay later originations went to borrowers with lower credit scores.

CFPB matched BNPL loan data to credit records: BNPL lenders approved 78% of 2022 loans to applicants with subprime or deep-subprime credit scores, and nearly two-thirds of BNPL loans went to borrowers with lower credit scores.

assertions.quote: Typical payment processors charge you 2 to 4%. Buy now pay later charges you eight, sometimes upwards of 10%

verdicts.note: Documented across CFPB, Federal Reserve, and provider disclosures; merchant fees of roughly 2-8% fund the interest-free consumer loan.
